pages.title: Your First Day
pages.text:
When you first spawn, all six nutrition bars start at a moderate level. You won't feel any effects immediately — but they will begin to decay.

Your priority on day one is to gather a variety of foods before the bars run dry.

pages.title: Early Food Sources
pages.text:
$(bold)Fruits:$() Berry bushes, apple-bearing trees, and melon patches.
$(bold)Vegetables:$() Carrots, potatoes, and beetroot from villages or the ground.
$(bold)Proteins:$() Cooked chicken, beef, or fish from nearby animals and rivers.

pages.title: More Early Sources
pages.text:
$(bold)Grains:$() Bread from village chests, or seeds to plant wheat immediately.
$(bold)Dairy:$() A bucket of milk from any cow covers the dairy group in a pinch.

pages.title: Setting Up a Farm
pages.text:
A small mixed farm is the most reliable long-term strategy. Plant wheat, carrots, potatoes, and beetroot early.

Keep a cow pen nearby for milk and cooked beef. Even a tiny farm covers four of the six groups with minimal effort.

pages.title: Cooking Matters
pages.text:
Raw meats count as Proteins, but their nutrition values are lower than their cooked equivalents. Always cook your meat when possible.

Some foods only register as their group when prepared — check tooltips if a food isn't filling the bar you expect.

pages.title: Diminishing Returns
pages.text:
Eating the same food repeatedly gives less nutrition each time due to $(bold)diminishing returns$(). Rotate through different foods within each group to maximize efficiency.

See the $(bold)How It Works$() chapter for the full details.

pages.title: End of Day One
pages.text:
Sleep when all six bars are above their threshold and wake up with the $(#52c252)Sleep Bonus$(). This is the ideal daily rhythm Nourished is designed around.

With a bit of preparation, staying balanced becomes second nature.

pages.title: Next Steps
pages.text:
